questions.prompt: Why is multimodal progress better described as coexisting families than as successive eras?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: A.** CLIP-like encoders serve retrieval, connectors retrofit existing LLMs, and unified/omni systems support generation or streaming output. A newer topology does not obsolete every earlier one.

options.text: Different families optimize different constraints and remain useful
Every new family fully preserves the architecture of the previous generation
Historical labels are unrelated to training and inference differences

questions.explanation: **Correct answer: B.** The module’s KV accounting applies to visual positions inside ordinary decoder self-attention. Cross-attention or external visual memory needs different accounting.

options.text: With any ViT encoder, even when it connects through cross-attention
When visual positions enter the decoder self-attention stream
Only when the language decoder also generates images

questions.prompt: How much KV memory do 1,296 visual positions require at 128 KiB per position?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: B.** 1,296·128 KiB = 162 MiB. A resampler does not change that value if position count and KV format stay fixed. Reducing positions changes total KV; cross-attention requires accounting for a different storage path.

questions.prompt: Which resource does a Q-Former or resampler primarily reduce?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: C.** Learned queries extract a bounded set of representations from a larger feature grid. This creates a bottleneck while reducing LLM context length.

options.text: The parameter count of every vision-encoder layer
The bandwidth of a separate audio decoder
The number of visual positions passed to the language model

questions.prompt: Why does freezing an LLM not remove all backward work when training its projector?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: A.** Frozen weights need no weight gradients or optimizer state, but the loss must remain differentiable with respect to the projector output.

options.text: The projector still needs gradients through input activations
Every LLM weight is still updated
Freezing doubles visual sequence length

questions.explanation: **Correct answer: A.** Position encoding preserves geometry. Resizing, tiling, spatial merging, temporal sampling, and pruning determine token count.

questions.prompt: How can a unified model remain internally modular?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: B.** Janus separates visual pathways, InternVL-U uses an MMDiT head, and Thinker–Talker has a speech decoder. A unified product does not require one internal representation.

questions.prompt: Why does a large context window not solve long-video understanding by itself?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: C.** Two hours at 1 fps and 576 tokens per frame produce 4.15 million tokens. Sampling, temporal pooling, and event selection determine retained evidence.

options.text: Video frames cannot be represented as discrete visual tokens

questions.prompt: Why does patch_layout reject silent integer truncation?
questions.explanation: **Correct answer: B.** Integer division could hide an incomplete patch. A processor may explicitly resize or pad; accounting for padded regions follows its actual interface and does not always require a separate pixel mask.

options.text: To make every image automatically square before tokenization
To avoid losing a border without explicit resize or padding
To force spatial merging to use one universal factor

options.text: Similarity between image and caption embeddings
Norm preservation through the connector MLP
Mutual consistency of the two operations on the tested input
